best/liska.name: Fox
profile: Foxes live in forests, along meadow edges and near human settlements. They seek shelter in burrows, among roots or in dense vegetation. They hunt small animals for food, but also eat fruit and readily available scraps. A narrow trail, a print in the mud or a russet tail disappearing into the undergrowth may reveal their presence.

A fox is curious, quick to learn and cautious. It often travels alone, although it may share its territory with a mate and cubs. Rather than face a direct confrontation, it prefers speed, cover and an evasive move; it usually bites in self-defence when it cannot escape. Its Dodge ability helps it resist one declared attack during a combat.

In an adventure, a fox might carry supplies away from camp or lead the party to a den in forgotten ruins. The heroes may discover that the apparently cheeky thief is simply gathering food for its cubs. Patient observation is often more useful than a chase.
best/liska.abilityEffect: Once per combat, after an attack target is declared, gains +2 Defense against that attack.

best/vlk.name: Wolf
profile: Wolves live in forests, on open plains and in mountain areas where they can find prey and enough space. A pack is usually a family group that works together to hunt and care for its young. Tracks left by several animals and distant howling may suggest that the party has entered their territory.

Wolves are alert, quick to learn and capable of cooperation. They usually avoid people; they may defend themselves when protecting their young, cornered or left with no other choice. A lone wolf does not necessarily mean an immediate attack, but it is worth watching the surroundings. In the game, Pack Attack applies if another wolf has attacked the same target during that round.

The party might discover an injured animal, a den they have approached too closely or a trail shared by wolves and people. A good solution may involve going around their territory and removing the cause of the conflict. A wolf is not automatically an evil opponent: its behaviour should fit the situation.

strings.Pokud stejný cíl v tomto kole napadl ale: If at least one other wolf attacked the same target this round, this wolf gains +1 to its final Attack result.

best/krysa.name: Rat
profile: Rats stay wherever they can find food, warmth and shelter: in cellars, granaries, stables and underground passages. Tiny tracks, gnawed sacks and rustling behind a wall reveal their presence. They often share hiding places and remember safe routes to supplies.

They are cautious and quick, usually trying to hide from a larger opponent. They may bite when cornered or protecting a nest; a large cluster of rats can block a narrow passage for the party. Agility is their strength, while their small size limits their physical strength. In the game, Slip Away helps them avoid a subsequent physical hit.

An encounter need not end in combat. The party can secure its supplies, find a hole in the wall or lure the rats away from the route. If unusually large numbers gather in one place, they may point to hidden food or a forgotten passage.

strings.1× za souboj po obdržení zranění získá +: Once per combat, after taking damage, gains +2 Defense against the next physical attack.

best/netopyr.name: Bat
profile: Bats rest in caves, hollow trees and abandoned towers. At dusk they set out in search of food; ordinary small bats mainly hunt insects. They navigate in darkness using echoes of their own calls and may share their shelters in large colonies.

They are not natural enemies of the heroes. A disturbed colony can, however, turn a quiet passage into a chaotic stream of wings and sounds. A bat is agile in the air but physically weak. Its Flight ability increases physical defense against melee attacks only while it can actually fly.

The Game Master can use bats as a sign of a nearby cave or an open route outside. The heroes can let the animals fly past undisturbed and continue instead of drawing their weapons. Unusual behavior in a colony may provide a clue that something is disturbing its shelter.

strings.Dokud může létat, získává +1 FO proti út: While it can fly, gains +1 PDEF against melee attacks.

best/divoka-kocka.name: Wildcat
profile: The wildcat lives in quiet forests, thickets and rocky places where it can find small prey and safe hiding places. It is usually solitary and moves silently; a paw print, scratches on a trunk or a brief flash of eyes among the branches may reveal its presence.

It is alert and patient, preferring escape to an unnecessary confrontation. When defending its young or unable to retreat, however, it can spring forward fiercely and use both claws and teeth. It relies on mobility and surprise. Its Pounce ability is most useful at the start of combat.

By following a wildcat, the party might discover a quiet shelter, a small trail or a place recently disturbed by another creature. Earning its trust requires patience and distance; it is not a tame house cat, and approaching too quickly may frighten it.

strings.V prvním kole souboje má +1 k výslednému: Gains +1 to the final Attack result during the first round of combat.

best/toulavy-pes.name: Stray Dog
profile: A stray dog is often a lost or abandoned human companion. It wanders around villages, markets and roads in search of food, water and a dry place to rest. Some dogs live alone, while others join a small group to seek safety together.

It can recognize moods, familiar smells and simple human behavior. Hunger or bad experiences may make it distrustful, but not every stray dog is aggressive. Its barking may warn of danger, guard a shelter it has found or draw attention to something the party has not yet noticed. It has no special combat ability.

An encounter may begin a search for its owner or an effort to help an entire village. The dog might guard a lost backpack, return to an empty house or follow the trail of someone it knows. The heroes should respect its distance and earn its trust gradually, without trying to grab it by force.

best/divoke-prase.name: Wild Boar
profile: A wild boar searches for food in forests, thickets and along the edges of fields. Churned earth, tracks in wet mud and bark rubbed off trees reveal its movements. Females with young stay in groups, while an adult male may roam alone.

It has an excellent sense of smell, a powerful body and can quickly gather speed. It usually prefers to retreat, but may attack fiercely if surprised at close range or defending its young. Surrounding it is unwise. Its Charge ability strengthens its first attack only if it actually has room for a running start.

In an adventure, a herd might block a forest path or forage somewhere hunger has driven it to. The heroes can retreat, find another route or discover why the animals have left their usual territory. Freshly churned ground may also uncover a lost object or an old entrance underground.

strings.V prvním kole, pokud může zaútočit po ro: During the first round, if it can attack after a running start, gains +2 to its final Attack result.

best/jedovaty-had.name: Venomous Snake
profile: A venomous snake hides under stones, among roots, in tall grass or in warm cracks in the rock. This bestiary entry represents a game creature with a venomous bite, rather than every snake in the real world. It usually lives alone, seeking prey and a safe shelter.

It is inconspicuous and can wait motionless for a long time. It generally does not attack a larger creature as prey; danger mainly arises when it is startled or cornered. The party should watch where it steps and reaches. Its game venom only takes effect after a bite that causes damage, and the subsequent effect is specified precisely in its ability.

A snake may guard a location simply because it has chosen to shelter there. Taking another route or leaving it room is often wiser than fighting. In a story, shed skin and small tracks might lead to a warm spring or a room that has remained unopened for years.

strings.Pokud uštknutí způsobí alespoň 1 zranění: If a bite deals at least 1 damage, the target loses 1 additional HP at the end of each of the next 2 rounds; this effect does not stack.
